systems.title: Werner’s Nomenclature of Colours
systems.about: Abraham Gottlob Werner’s colour scheme for minerals, extended by Patrick Syme, Edinburgh, 1814. Each colour is keyed to an animal, a plant and a mineral.

systems.title: Color Standards and Color Nomenclature
systems.about: Robert Ridgway, an American ornithologist, Washington DC, 1912. Printed swatches made to name the colours of birds, and more.

systems.title: RAL colour standard
systems.about: A German industrial standard for colour, first issued in 1927. Names in English translation.

systems.title: A Dictionary of Color Combinations
systems.about: After Sanzo Wada’s volumes of colour combinations, Japan, 1930s. Names in English translation.

systems.title: Polychromie architecturale
systems.about: Le Corbusier’s colour keyboards for Salubra wallpapers, 1931 and 1959.

systems.title: Universal Color Language
systems.about: The Inter-Society Color Council and the US National Bureau of Standards, 1955. Each name is a modifier and a hue.

systems.title: Named colours of the web
systems.about: The colour keywords of HTML and CSS, carried over from the X11 colour list.

systems.title: xkcd colour survey
systems.about: Randall Munroe’s online colour-naming survey, 2010. Names typed by people on the web.

systems.key: Many Languages Many Colors (UW): eleven languages
systems.title: Many Languages, Many Colors
systems.about: An online colour-naming survey from the University of Washington’s Interactive Data Lab. Here: Korean 32, Chinese 21, French 11, German 10, Spanish 10, Portuguese 5, Russian 4, Dutch 4, Finnish 3, Swedish 3, Polish 2, Romanian 1.

systems.title: Traditional colours of China
systems.about: Chinese colour names with pinyin, from a single CSV file by GitHub user ItMarki. Who compiled it, and from which sources, is not verified.

systems.title: Traditional colours of Japan
systems.about: From Wikipedia’s list of traditional colours of Japan. The names are historical; the hex values were attached by its editors, citing Japanese colour references.
